scope: Corollary 2.5 (Buffered and small-patch comparisons) of the manuscript “Buffered comparison and stopping-band resolution in critical Ising” (preprints/Buffered-comparison-and-stopping-band-resolution-in-critical-Ising-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 218 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d5167e3fe5fb85f4), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 6-7. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix c > 0. There is Kc < ∞ such that, on the square lattice, I ⊆ z + BR and J ⊆ (z + B(1+c)R)c imply pointwise density ratios in [K−1 c , Kc] for the conditional laws in Lemma 2.2. Other common pins may occur anywhere off I ∪ J. There are absolute K < ∞ and δ > 0 such that, if I ⊆ z +Bw, J ⊆ (z +BR)c, and R ≥ 8w ≥ 8, the logarithm of every such conditional density ratio has absolute value at most K(w/R)δ . (2.3) In particular the total variation distance is at most K′(w/R)δ, and the expectation difference of a bounded test function is at most 2K′∥h∥∞(w/R)δ. No free neighborhood of the source patch I is required. 6 The buffered comparison also holds between laws from different domains, including plane, torus, or cylinder laws, whenever their common collar is an isometric square-lattice chart and all differing data lie beyond it. It holds after applying the same conditional randomization kernel to local spins, in particular internal Edwards–Sokal bond sampling.
